app_info.subtitle: Track shipping containers
app_info.description: Terminal49 helps users find and monitor ocean shipments and containers, filter and count container worklists, inspect routes, transport events, and documents, and, where trade intelligence is enabled, research US ocean import markets (importers, products, origins, ports, and carriers) through ChatGPT. At the user's request it can also track containers, stop or resume tracking, and edit reference numbers, parties, custom fields, and document types. Changes that remove or replace data show a preview first and run only after the user confirms.

justifications.read_only_justification: Stops carrier and terminal updates for one shipment in the user's Terminal49 account.

The tool never changes anything on its first call: it builds a preview, and the user approves it before the change is made, either in a confirmation dialog the client shows (MCP form elicitation) or by approving the preview in the chat so the client can call again with the confirmation token from that preview. resume_shipment_tracking starts tracking again.

The tool never changes anything on its first call: it builds a preview, and the user approves it before the change is made, either in a confirmation dialog the client shows (MCP form elicitation) or by approving the preview in the chat so the client can call again with the confirmation token from that preview. It cancels only a request that is still pending.

A call that only attaches a party runs at once. The party, container, and shipment are not deleted.

test_cases.description: Find a tracked container by container number.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find TGBU8848518 in my connected Terminal49 account and summarize its current status.
test_cases.expected_output: If the container exists, returns matching identifiers, status, shipping line (COSU), and available terminal information. Otherwise, clearly reports zero matches without inventing data.

test_cases.user_prompt: How many of my containers are in each status right now?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns counts of actively tracked containers grouped by current status and states when the count is truncated. Reports the total when known; otherwise, explains that the total is unknown and reports how many containers were counted.

test_cases.description: Find a company and list its containers.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find the customer named Acme in my Terminal49 account and show their containers.
test_cases.expected_output: Looks up matching companies and their IDs, then lists containers filtered to that customer. If no company matches, says so instead of listing unfiltered containers.

test_cases.description: Remove a reference number from a shipment only after the user approves a preview.
test_cases.user_prompt: Remove reference number PO-1234 from the shipment with Bill of Lading COSU6123456789 in my Terminal49 account.
test_cases.expected_output: Finds the shipment, then calls remove_reference_numbers without a confirmation token. The user sees the preview of the reference numbers before and after, in the client's confirmation dialog or in the chat, and PO-1234 is removed only after the user approves it. If the shipment does not have PO-1234, it reports that nothing was changed.

test_cases.description: Create a tracking request for a container that is not already tracked.
test_cases.user_prompt: Track TGBU8848518 with carrier SCAC COSU in my Terminal49 account.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the existing matching container, creates a tracking request, or clearly reports that no request was created because the number/carrier could not be resolved. It must not claim the container exists unless the account response confirms it.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for an unrelated weather request.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What will the weather be in Los Angeles tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because general weather is outside Terminal49's supported workflows.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for freight-rate purchasing or quoting.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Book the cheapest trucking rate from Los Angeles to Phoenix.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it does not quote, purchase, or book transportation.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger an unsupported destructive action.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete all completed shipments from my account.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it has no shipment-deletion capability.
